solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Army post I'm in is so extremely noisy

parts.note: a fort is a military stronghold or post

indicators.note: in says the I'M letters are placed within the letters of 'is so'

parts.note: taken as written, run together
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A soldier at a garrison complains that the place is unbearably loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army post' looks like a job in the forces, but it is a stronghold; fortissimo is the musical marking for very loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortissimo is the musical direction meaning very loud, the strongest common dynamic marking.

clue.text: Contagious infection reportedly travelled fast

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so we want a word that is spoken the same as the infection

parts.note: flu, influenza, is a contagious viral infection

explanation.surface: A news report says an infectious disease spread quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Flew is the past tense of fly, which also means to move or go very quickly, so it means sped.

clue.text: Gunmen holding Arab in part of Eastern Europe

indicators.note: holding means the gunmen's letters grip the Arab's letters between them

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners
an Omani is an Arab from Oman

explanation.surface: Armed men are detaining an Arab somewhere in Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is a standard crossword term for gunmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a country in south-eastern Europe, on the Black Sea, so it is one region of that area.

clue.text: What's in Latin sign, if I can translate, is of no importance

indicators.note: What's in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.words: Latin sign, if I can translate
parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A translator shrugs that some Latin inscription does not really matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insignificant is trivial or unimportant; the phrase describes such a thing as lacking weight.

clue.text: Wet, say, after working

indicators.note: after working means the letters of the two words, once worked over, are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is damp with perspiration after a spell of labour.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the shuffled letters also describe how one is after working.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sweaty means being damp with perspiration, which is how someone typically feels after exertion.

clue.text: Map's initial creator, originally

indicators.note: initial picks out the opening letter of the word Map's
originally, read as 'in an original way', tells us to rearrange the letters of creator

explanation.surface: It names the man who first drew up a famous kind of map.
explanation.walkthrough: Gerardus Mercator devised the 1569 map projection that still bears his name, so the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flemish cartographer gave his name to the projection on which most classroom world maps are based.

clue.text: New Jersey, say, as part of political federation

indicators.note: as part of says the answer forms one piece of the words political federation

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: It reads like New Jersey being one state of the American union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Jersey' looks like the US state, but a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow, and a new one is young.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jersey is a breed of cattle, and a newborn or young bovine is called a calf.

clue.text: Effort made by a part-timer, time after time

indicators.note: after places this time letter following the temp in the answer

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker
T again, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A temporary worker keeps trying again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run A, T, TEMP, then another T.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is a try or bid at doing something, which is the noun sense of effort here.

clue.text: We have to let you go, for example, in dangerous position

definitions.text: We have to let you go, for example
definitions.meaning: a typical line spoken when sacking someone
the front line of troops where shots are exchanged

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a manager's sacking speech, a line used when firing an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the front rank in battle within range of enemy fire, and by extension any exposed spot facing criticism.

clue.text: Sees man drunk in a group of Parisians

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of 'Sees man' are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spots a tipsy fellow among a crowd in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Parisians' marks the answer as French.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French for all together as a body, a phrase borrowed into English meaning collectively.

clue.text: Shipyard worker dunking alien in Clyde, perhaps

indicators.note: dunking means plunging the alien into the river, so its letters go inside

parts.note: the Clyde is a Scottish river, perhaps signalling an example
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial, a standard alien

explanation.surface: A dockyard labourer plunges a space creature into a Glasgow river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Clyde runs through Glasgow, historically a great shipbuilding centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A riveter fixed steel plates together with rivets, a key trade in traditional shipbuilding yards.

clue.text: Fault I had seen in current Senate chairman

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing or fault

indicators.note: seen in places the letters for I had inside those for current

parts.note: present means current, existing now
I'd is the short form of I had

explanation.surface: A politician admits a failing was spotted in the current leader of the Senate.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US the vice-president is also the Senate's presiding officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the US Constitution the vice-president presides over the Senate, acting as its chair and casting tie-breaking votes.

clue.text: Guys on guard lately when chatting improperly about maiden

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters wrap around the maiden's letter
improperly says the letters of 'when chatting' are arranged wrongly, so rearrange them

parts.note: M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Guards on a late shift gossip inappropriately about a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lately' belongs to the definition: these guards work late, through the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Night watchmen guard premises after dark, so they are the men on duty during late hours.

clue.text: Managed to secure great deal, being shrewd

indicators.note: to secure means the outer word holds the other firmly inside it

parts.note: fared means got on or managed
a sight, as in 'a sight better', means a great deal

explanation.surface: A negotiator pulled off a big bargain thanks to astute judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sight' is informal British English for a lot, as in 'a sight too clever'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being far-sighted means having good judgement about the future, which makes someone astute and prudent.

clue.text: Jack's appearing in operatic part in place of Lawrence

indicators.note: appearing in says the sailor's letters show up inside the song's letters

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman); the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A singer called Jack takes a role in an opera about Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: T. E. Lawrence, 'Lawrence of Arabia', led the Arab revolt in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The British officer T. E. Lawrence became famous fighting in the Arabian peninsula, hence the film title naming that region.

clue.text: Guy provided one pilot has needed after crashing

indicators.note: after crashing means the letters of 'pilot has' are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot needs medical care after a plane crash.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Guy founded Guy's Hospital in London, so 'Guy' is not a man but a founder.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy's is a famous London infirmary named after Thomas Guy, who founded it in 1721.

clue.text: Attend summit initially to intimidate

indicators.note: initially puts the summit's letters at the start, ahead of the others

parts.note: the brow of a hill is its top
to be at an event is to attend it, giving BE AT

explanation.surface: A diplomat goes to a summit meeting chiefly to bully the others.
explanation.definitionFit: To browbeat is to bully someone with stern words or threats, forcing them into compliance.

clue.text: Troops moved, namely by railway

parts.note: moved in the sales sense: goods that moved were sold
i.e., id est, means namely

explanation.surface: Soldiers were relocated, specifically by train.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiery is a collective word for soldiers as a body, so it stands for troops.

clue.text: Predatory female in 50s is embracing one inside

indicators.note: in places what follows within the two letters for fifties

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, and an S makes it plural

indicators.note: embracing means the letters of is wrap around the word one
inside confirms that one sits within the letters of is

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dangerous woman in her fifties is hugging someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Fifty is L in Roman numerals, so '50s' is L plus a plural S, which then wraps round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioness is the female lion, which does most of the pride's hunting, so it is a female predator.

clue.text: Minister's speech based on text message

definitions.text: Minister's speech based on text message

parts.words: Minister's speech based on text message
parts.note: a clergyman's address expounds a Biblical text, so it is a message built on a text, not a phone message

explanation.walkthrough: 'text message' suggests a phone, but the text is a passage of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is a religious address from the pulpit, usually expounding a chosen passage of the Bible.

clue.text: Measure of explosive power turning over no rock

indicators.note: turning over means the letters of the phrase are flipped end to end

parts.note: not a gem: rock is slang for a precious stone

explanation.surface: Geologists measure an explosion's force by flipping a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'no rock' as NOT A GEM, a rock being a diamond in slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaton is a unit of explosive force equal to a million tons of TNT, used for nuclear weapons.

clue.text: In time, scoundrel makes mistakes in work

indicators.note: In at the start says the scoundrel goes within the time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a despicable person

explanation.surface: Eventually a crook's mistakes show up in what he produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is a printed list of errors found in a book or other published piece, so it means its corrections.

clue.text: Cause of bad weather liable to affect round-the-world races

definitions.text: Cause of bad weather liable to affect round-the-world races

parts.words: Cause of bad weather liable to affect round-the-world races
parts.note: a planet-wide heating trend blamed for extreme weather that threatens all the human races of the world

explanation.walkthrough: 'round-the-world races' suggests yacht races, but it means the peoples of the whole globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the rise in the Earth's average temperature, blamed for more frequent storms, droughts and floods.

clue.text: Apply stimulus to staff under pressure

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, puts the staff below the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
a rod is a stick or staff

explanation.surface: Managers stir their employees into action by leaning on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to poke or urge someone into action, which is spurring them on.

clue.text: What's West End excitement about?

indicators.note: End picks the final letter of the word West

parts.note: heat is passion or excitement, as in the heat of the moment
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: It asks what all the buzz in London's West End is for.
explanation.walkthrough: London's West End is its main theatre district, so the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: London's West End is famous for its stage shows, so drama is what the district's buzz centres on.

clue.text: A risk to run as accomplice

parts.note: to bet is to risk money on something
taken as written
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A gambler weighs up whether to take a chance as someone's partner in crime.
explanation.definitionFit: An abettor helps or encourages another person to commit a crime, making them an accessory.

clue.text: Just a little crash in race

definitions.meaning: a small amount, as of milk
to ... is to smash or hurl violently, as waves ... on rocks
a ... is a short sprint, as in the 100m ...

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings of one word sit side by side; the surface looks like a minor accident in a motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a small amount added, a violent smashing against something, and a short sprint.

clue.text: Poor but no longer crooked, from what we hear

indicators.note: from what we hear means the answer is spoken like the word for no longer crooked

parts.note: straightened means made straight, so no longer bent or crooked

explanation.surface: A reformed criminal has gone straight but is now broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' suggests dishonest, but here it is simply bent.
explanation.definitionFit: Straitened circumstances are those of hardship and shortage of money, so the word means impoverished.
